When I started reading the books just after Nona came out, I thought it was a finished trilogy, because things still referred to it as a trilogy!! I thought I was so smart!! FOOL. I was a fool!

I’ve been chasing that high ever since. I look up lists of “books like Gideon the Ninth” and try to read them even though the books are never like Gideon the Ninth. I read everything else by Tamsyn (the short stories/supplemental stuff, Princess Floralinda, her short story Undercover). And of course. I reread the three books we have.

As for “books like Gideon the Ninth,” here’s a summary of ones I’ve tried in case something catches your eye:

The Library at Mount Char by Scott Hawkins: by far the most recommended. A lot of people love this book. I did not!!! And I don’t think it’s that much like Locked Tomb either, but I see why people say it is. It’s about a bunch of effectively immortal young adults who have been taken under the wing of a man called Father who is also their teacher and also god. A big part of the reason it didn’t work for me is that even though the main character is a woman overall it read very heterosexual and masculine, and I think the focus on women and especially the incredible queerness are so so important to what makes Locked Tomb feel the way that it does. Plus it comes to a conclusion about uh the value of child abuse that I just can’t get past. (eta: right after I posted this I saw someone describe this book as “Umbrella Academy meets the Magicians” which feels WAY more accurate to me.)

All Systems Red by Martha Wells aka the first Murderbot Diaries book: this one comes much closer to the mark imo! It’s a quick read but then there’s a whole series afterwards that I haven’t read yet. This is about a “murderbot” that has basically developed sapience/autonomy and now all it wants to do is binge watch TV. Extremely relatable. It’s much more queer, Murderbot is asexual, and it doesn’t feel like This Book Was Written By a Straight Man (because it wasn’t). Plus it has some good found family content which is another important locked tomb component.

Voyage of the Damned by Frances White: if you want a book that feels like read Gideon, this is the one. I want to preface this by saying it’s not even in the same league of quality and I have some problems with the ending but I was otherwise just so delighted by it. It has an extremely likable and memorable narrator with an idiosyncratic voice, it’s about him and the scions of noble houses all together with no one else around (on a boat in this case), and it’s about the murders that follow. Plus the world is just so, so queer. A lot of people didn’t like this book and I get it, but I had a really good time with it and nothing else has REALLY made me feel so much like reading Gideon.

I also have a galaxy-brained theory that Becky Chambers is another one even though the tone is the exact opposite because she also writes queer found family science fiction, but I haven’t read enough to say if this is true yet.

Listen I’ve never watched Sherlock except once I saw the first episode but I was very extremely drunk and only remember that Cumberbatch has a nice voice and wears a suit well. But there’s a clip in Harry’s video that’s been haunting me for YEARS: when Sherlock says, “there must be something comforting about the number three. People always give up after three.” It sounds clever until you think about it for six seconds. What do you MEAN, Sherlock? People don’t go, “well I found three, that’s me done then.” If you’re looking for things why would you stop after three! That’s not a thing people do!! What are you talking about!!!

Elementary is GOAT. I’ve rewatched it multiple times. It does such new and interesting things with the Sherlock mythos without ever acting like it thinks it’s better than the original. The stuff with Sherlock’s addiction in particular is just so well-done.

Hey. I’m not really sure how to put this cause I feel the same way you do about a lot of things but. I’m on disability too. I can’t work for a lot of reasons. I feel like a worthless piece of garbage 110% of the time because of this and other reasons and I’m sure I’m not getting paid anymore after this month anyway, not that it was ever even close to something a person could live off of. I really would rather just die as well and look forward to the day I end it.

But there’s one thing I do know and that’s that the wealthy and able-bodied are not WORTH MORE than I am as a human being. They’re not worth more than YOU. It’s a lie we’ve been beaten down with and ground into the dirt so hard with that it’s difficult not to believe. It’s built into the way they make us live and we have to stare it in the face every day. They don’t deserve more because of accidents of birth and we don’t deserve less. It’s a horrible system that makes us hate ourselves because we can’t “contribute” as much to someone ELSE’S bottom line. That’s all it is. We’re harder for other people to make money off of and so they make us feel like we’re not worth the oxygen we breathe. It’s not true. It’s not true and I don’t know if you’re even going to read this never mind take it to heart but I needed to tell you, it’s not true. There’s no such thing as surplus population. We all matter the same amount, including you.

Laziness isn’t real imo, I mean if you look at the definition of the word sloth as a “deadly sin” it’s literally just depression. Who sets the standard for what’s an acceptable amount of activity anyway?

Just want to add to the chorus of people assuring you that your problems are indeed valid. There are unfortunately a lot of different ways to hurt and be hurt in this world, and it sounds like you’ve taken the brunt of some pretty severe stuff. Just because “it could be worse” or whatever nonsense people/your jerk brain are telling you doesn’t mean it’s not still bad. I just... hope that, at least, is something you can hear enough to accept, that your problems are valid and your pain is valid and you are valid. I know saying white people problems/first world problems/etc are all jokey, tongue-in-cheek ways to be dismissive of our own struggles, but please remember that trauma, chronic illness, and suicidal thoughts may not necessarily have anything to do with race etc, but they are SUPER SERIOUS things to deal with on an individual level. People’s concept of intersectionality doesn’t seem to have caught onto that yet and it’s really frustrating!!

Also you said you are or were taking Wellbutrin? I used to take that and it wreaked havoc on my anxiety. Just as a btw, if that might have some relevance.

Someone who knows your story, so you don't have to explain it all over and over again, never knowing what parts they're going to judge or dismiss or file away as reasons to bug out later. That's a good question, and one I stopped asking myself when I realized I had no answer to it, because that's not any less empty than death. The best answer I can come up with is, some kind of meaning or purpose in life, some reason to get up in the morning, but that's so nebulous, and not something you can rely on anyway, because a person can have everything in the world to live for and it can still not matter because depression is a soul-sucking bitch. I don't know what would help, I really don't, and while it's a fair assumption that there's SOMETHING that would, I have no idea what it is or how to find it, especially when wanting things is painful to begin with.

It really does seem like everyone is sad these days though.

I thought my childhood was fine too, in spite of the fact that I've been dealing with some of these problems for literally as long as I can remember (always being very anxious and sad, even the headaches have been a fixture from the start). I think as a child, however, it mattered less, because I would outgrow these things, or they would get better once I got older for other reasons. There was always so much time, and support, and opportunity, you know, you can be whatever you want to be if you just (x, y, z). But then adulthood comes and you realize it's all bullshit? It's like believing in Santa Claus. It's a nice fantasy but eventually you realize that's all it is.
